A drum mic hears the whole kit. Between kick hits, the kick mic is picking up the snare, the hats and the
cymbals: **bleed**. A **gate** closes the channel when the level falls below a threshold, and opens it again
when the drum is hit.

## The X32 gate

Press **Gate** on the channel strip to switch it on and turn its threshold knob. On the screen (View) there is
more:

- **Mode**: `GATE` closes all the way down to the Range. `EXP2`, `EXP3`, `EXP4` are **expanders**: below the
  threshold they turn down gradually (by 2, 3 or 4 times as much as the signal drops), which sounds more natural.
  (`DUCK` does the opposite, turning down when something else is loud; not used here.)
- **Threshold** (−80 to 0 dB): the level that opens it. Above the bleed, below the quietest hit you want.
- **Range** (3–60 dB): how far it closes. 60 dB is nearly silent; 10–20 dB just tucks the bleed down.
- **Attack** (0–120 ms): how fast it opens. On drums, as fast as possible, or the start of each hit is lost.
- **Hold** (up to 2 s): how long it stays open after the level drops.
- **Release** (5 ms – 4 s): how fast it closes. Too short chops the drum's ring; too long lets the bleed back in.

The fader strip's **gate light** shows when it's working.

## Try it: the kick

<div class="lk" data-w="strip" data-source="kick" data-show="pre gate fader" data-goal="gate"
  data-tries="No gate:gate=0;Threshold too high:gate=1,gthr=-14;Threshold too low:gate=1,gthr=-45;Slow attack:gate=1,gthr=-30,gatt=30;Good:gate=1,gthr=-30,gatt=0,ghold=20,grel=120"></div>

Watch the strip at the bottom: the grey line is the level the gate sees, the dashed green line its threshold.
The kicks are the tall spikes; the snare bleed the smaller ones in between. Put the threshold between them.
Careful: one kick near the end is played softly (a ghost note), and it must still get through.

## Try it: the toms

Toms ring for a long time, and a tom mic sits right next to the snare and under the cymbals.

<div class="lk" data-w="strip" data-source="toms" data-show="pre gate fader" data-goal="gate"
  data-tries="No gate:gate=0;Release too short:gate=1,gthr=-24,ghold=2,grel=10;Gentle expander:gate=1,gmode=1,gthr=-17,grange=20,ghold=60,grel=300"></div>

Here the **Release** matters: set it short and every tom hit is cut to a click. A longer Hold and Release keep
the ring. Try **EXP3** with a Range of about 20 dB too: it's less "on/off".

<div class="sk-tip">Gating every drum isn't always right. In a small room the kit is loud on its own, and
the bleed is part of the sound. Gate the toms and maybe the kick; leave the overheads alone.</div>
